title: Metrics, Logs, Traces & Exemplars
summary: Observability explains system behavior from outside: metrics for aggregates, logs for events, traces for request journeys, exemplars linking them. Designing telemetry is part of system design.

sections.title: Three pillars — and linking them
paragraphs: Metrics alert and dashboard. Logs debug specifics. Traces show causal paths across services. Exemplars and trace IDs connect a metric spike to example requests.

sections.title: Golden signals and SLIs
paragraphs: Latency, traffic, errors, saturation. Define SLIs from user journeys, not only host CPU.

sections.title: Cardinality and cost
paragraphs: High-cardinality labels explode metric cost. Sample traces; structure logs; drop noisy fields. Telemetry has a budget.

sections.title: Instrumentation practice
paragraphs: Propagate context across async boundaries. Prefer OpenTelemetry. Make dashboards and alerts owned by the same team as the service.

deepDive.title: Metrics, Logs, Traces & Exemplars — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Metrics, Logs, Traces & Exemplars in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Metrics, Logs, Traces & Exemplars — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Metrics, Logs, Traces & Exemplars include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Metrics, Logs, Traces & Exemplars — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Metrics, Logs, Traces & Exemplars intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

whyItMatters: You cannot operate what you cannot see — and blind systems fail longer.
reflectionQuestions: Can you jump from an SLO burn alert to an example trace in two clicks?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
